claim_ceiling: Oracle-free greedy iterative decompression (try brotli->gzip until neither succeeds, MAX_DEPTH=5, no SHA256 oracle) produces byte-identical output to ground truth for 100% of cached responses (330/330 cached-path obs, 240/240 primary 48x5 HIT, 45/45 depth 3-5, 30/30 >100KB, 15/15 identity, 6/6 stability) through a byte-preserving local nginx 1.24.0 proxy_cache reverse proxy (proxy_cache_key $request_uri, 5m validity, gzip off, HTTP/1.1, no TLS) in front of a Python origin with Cache-Control: public, max-age=300, when HIT is fresh (within max-age, 1-3s populate->test). DYNAMIC and HIT wire bytes are byte-identical for 48/48 cells, so decompressed outputs are identical. This closes the parent HIT gap only for nginx-class byte-preserving caches with the tested payload matrix (JSON/HTML/BINARY, entropy 4.66-7.70, GZIP-OUTER/BROTLI-OUTER, chunk 8192/32, 4 AE variants, SEED=44). Does NOT extend to: Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai/CloudFront edge HIT behavior (re-encoding, stale-expired, 304, H2/H3, concurrent load, multi-edge, or byte-transforming caches), production CDN HIT serving, or performance economics.
